questions.question: What is the Earth's axis, and what is rotation?
questions.expected_answer: The Earth's axis is an imaginary line through the middle of the Earth, from the North Pole to the South Pole. Rotation is the Earth spinning around its axis, like a top. The Earth rotates from west to east once in about twenty-four hours, which is one day. All the other planets rotate too, but at different speeds.

questions.question: Explain how the Earth's rotation causes day and night, and why different countries have day and night at different times.
questions.expected_answer: The Sun can only light up the half of the Earth facing it, so that half has day and the other half has night. As the Earth rotates, each place moves from the dark half into the light, which is sunrise, and back into the dark, which is sunset. Because the Earth is round and spinning, places on different sides face the Sun at different times, so when it is evening in South Africa it is midday in New York.

questions.question: Why does the Sun seem to rise in the east and set in the west, and how does a shadow stick show the Earth's rotation?
questions.expected_answer: The Earth spins from west to east, so each morning our part of the Earth turns towards the Sun and it comes into view on the eastern horizon, and in the evening we turn away and it disappears in the west. The Sun is not really moving across the sky. A shadow stick's shadow is long and points west in the morning, is shortest and points south at midday in South Africa, and is long and points east in the afternoon, because the Earth is turning.
